maria (eng-platform): quick question — SRE hit a surprise yesterday where a canary was at 0.5% but feature flag said enabled=true for 10% users. who is the source of truth for traffic splits in a rollout?
ben (product): ugh classic layering confusion. product expects feature flags to control exposure; platform expects rollout policy to own traffic arithmetic.
lee (devex): do we have a precedence doc anywhere? people keep editing the console flag and the runtime policy separately.
sam (eng-runtime): short answer: runtime policy should be authoritative for routing/guards. flags are semantics for product surface. but our code isn't enforcing that consistently.
maria (eng-platform): @sam can you point to the code path? is it console -> api -> runtime merge? or runtime ignores console splits?
sam (eng-runtime): current flow (simplified): deploy console PR -> console writes FlagStore -> ControlPlane publishes RolloutPolicy -> Runtime fetches RolloutPolicy + FlagStore and does a naive merge where FlagStore wins on non-empty values. that was a quick win.
ben (product): that's the problem — product sets flags during experiments and expects runtime to respect them. but runtime merge means you can override a rollout guard by setting a flag. not ideal.
maria (eng-platform): proposal: make RolloutPolicy take precedence for routing keys and guards, flags map to feature toggles (behavior) only. We should make that explicit in the API and console UX.
lee (devex): can we add a fast fail for ambiguous configs? something like: if both sides set traffic_split_pct, console shows a warning and runtime logs an error until resolved? :warning:

sam (eng-runtime): quick config snippet of what we currently do:
```
// current runtime merge (pseudocode)
policy = fetchRolloutPolicy()
flag = fetchFlag()
result.traffic_split = flag.traffic_split || policy.traffic_split
result.guard = flag.guard || policy.guard
```

sam (eng-runtime): proposed change:
```
// enforce policy precedence
policy = fetchRolloutPolicy()
flag = fetchFlag()
if (policy.traffic_split != null) result.traffic_split = policy.traffic_split
else result.traffic_split = flag.traffic_split
// guard is policy-only
result.guard = policy.guard || null
```

ben (product): +1 to policy owning routing. product flags should be "soft" controls for behavior not traffic. this matches experiments model.
maria (eng-platform): ops question: how does this affect existing rollouts? we need migration and a UX affordance — console should surface when a flag is shadowing a policy.
lee (devex): UX idea: show a banner on rollout page: "Traffic split defined in policy — editing flag traffic will be ignored. Click to move config to policy." add a one-click "migrate to policy" that copies values. :sparkles:

deploy-bot: Canary created: rollout_id=rn-42, initial_split=0.5% (from flags), policy_split=null

sam (eng-runtime): deploy-bot just shows the exact problem. runtime pulled the flag split. recommend we ship policy-precedence patch + console warning in the same release window.

maria (eng-platform): plan: 1) sam makes runtime change to prefer policy for routing (PR) 2) lee adds console warning + migrate button (UX) 3) ben will run a comms note for PMs about flag vs policy semantics 4) schedule rollout for next week. any blockers?

ben (product): none from product, happy to help craft wording.

lee (devex): I'll prototype banner, putting a mock in #design tomorrow.

sam (eng-runtime): I'll open PR this afternoon, link to thread.

maria (eng-platform): thanks everyone. leaving this thread open until PRs are linked and a migration plan is in the release notes. :white_check_mark:
